checkpoints.title: Where did they come from?
checkpoints.question: From which IP address did the remote logon come?
hints: Look at logon events (4624 and 4625) in security-events.csv.
The same address appears in the failed attempts and in the successful logon.
checkpoints.success: Right. Every attempt came from that one address.

checkpoints.title: Did they get in?
checkpoints.question: What is the record number of the first successful logon from that address?
hints: Event ID 4624 is a successful logon.
It comes right after three 4625 records.
checkpoints.success: Right. Three failures, then a success: a password-guessing pattern.

checkpoints.title: When exactly?
checkpoints.question: At what UTC time (to the second) did that successful logon happen?
hints: Use the time_utc column of the record from checkpoint 2.
checkpoints.success: Right. Write that time in your timeline.

checkpoints.title: Which event ID?
checkpoints.question: Which event ID records the installation of a new service?
checkpoints.success: Right. 7045 means a service was installed.

checkpoints.title: What was left behind?
checkpoints.question: What is the full path of the program the new service runs?
hints: The image_path column holds the program path.
checkpoints.success: Right. A program in a Temp folder running as a service deserves a closer look.
